name: NinjaOne
description: NinjaOne is a unified IT operations platform that combines remote monitoring and management (RMM), automated patch management, backup, remote access, and service-desk ticketing for IT teams and managed service providers.
best_for: IT teams and managed service providers (MSPs) wanting to consolidate endpoint monitoring, patching, backup, and remote access into a single console.
features: Unified endpoint visibility and control across Windows, macOS, and Linux devices
Mobile device management (MDM) for iOS, iPadOS, and Android devices
AI-driven autonomous patch management to accelerate vulnerability remediation
Endpoint, server, and SaaS backup with compliance support
Built-in service desk with documentation and ticketing
Cross-platform scripting support (PowerShell, Bash, and shell commands)
pros: Single console spanning RMM, patching, backup, and remote access
SOC 2 compliant and ISO 27001:2022 certified, with FedRAMP Moderate Authorization for regulated environments (per NinjaOne's trust center)
cons: No published self-serve pricing — NinjaOne requires requesting a quote, and per-device cost depends on volume and contract terms

alternatives.name: Freshservice
alternatives.description: A cloud ITSM platform unifying service desk, IT asset management, and IT operations with Freddy AI-assisted ticket resolution.
alternatives.best_for: IT teams wanting a ticket-first ITSM service desk with transparent per-agent pricing rather than RMM-led endpoint monitoring.

alternatives.name: ServiceNow ITSM
alternatives.description: An enterprise IT service management suite built on the ServiceNow AI Platform, unifying incident, change, and problem management with autonomous AI agents.
alternatives.best_for: Large enterprises wanting ITSM unified with broader enterprise workflows rather than MSP-focused RMM.
strengths: Autonomous AI agents for routine requests

faq.question: Does NinjaOne publish its pricing?
faq.answer: No. NinjaOne uses per-device, volume-tiered pricing but does not publish exact rates on its site — you need to request a quote. It does offer a 14-day free trial.
